sources.title: Ismaël Castillo and Richard Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Annals of Statistics 41(4) (2013), 1999–2028
sources.locator: Full 30-page article fetched and inspected. Focused complete units: Definition 1 and §1.2, printed pp. 2003–2006 (PDF pp. 5–8); Condition 1 and full proof of Theorem 5, printed pp. 2013–2016 (PDF pp. 15–18); Theorem 7 statement (its proof is expressly omitted), printed p. 2017 (PDF p. 20); complete proof of Theorem 8 and proof of Theorem 9, printed pp. 2018–2020 (PDF pp. 21–23). The finite-coordinate proof in this batch is supplied locally rather than attributed to the omitted source proof.

contents.name: Definition 1: bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM centered at the white-noise observation
Definition 2 and §1.2: negative logarithmic Sobolev space, white-noise trace threshold, and canonical law
Condition 1 and complete proof of Theorem 5: coordinate posterior second moments and negative-Sobolev posterior contraction
Theorem 7: finite-dimensional total-variation BvM statement; source proof is expressly omitted
contents.reason: The source supplies the finite-dimensional target and hypotheses but omits its proof; this item proves the coordinate density limit directly by dominated convergence and an explicit product total-variation bound.

contents.name: Theorem 8 complete projection-and-tail proof and Theorem 9 product-prior assumptions and conclusion
Theorem 10 posterior-mean efficiency and §2 credible-set consequences
contents.reason: Posterior-mean efficiency and credible-set calibration are outside this pair's whole-posterior weak BvM claim and belong to the later functional-limits pair.

sources.title: Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models (Cambridge University Press, 2016)
sources.locator: Complete 705-page author-hosted monograph fetched; focused full-text units in Chapter 7, §7.3: Definition 7.3.10 and Condition 7.3.11, printed pp. 583–584 (PDF pp. 598–599); Theorem 7.3.12 and complete proof, printed pp. 584–586 (PDF pp. 599–601); Theorem 7.3.18 and complete proof, printed pp. 593–594 (PDF pp. 608–609); Theorem 7.3.19 and complete projection/tightness proof, printed pp. 595–596 (PDF pp. 610–611).

contents.name: Definition 7.3.10 and Condition 7.3.11: regular bases, scaled product priors, coefficient bound, density bounds, and second moment
Theorem 7.3.18 and complete finite-dimensional Gaussian white-noise BvM proof
contents.reason: The book verifies the finite-dimensional normal target; the local item expands the product-coordinate density argument so its total-variation steps are fully proved here.

contents.name: Theorem 7.3.19 weak BvM conclusion and complete finite-projection/tail-tightness proof
Theorem 7.3.20 multiscale M0(w) BvM theorem and stronger sub-Gaussian coefficient assumption
contents.reason: The controlling BCS-16 design selects the negative-Sobolev H(delta) result and its bounded-second-moment density condition; the separate multiscale M0(w) model and its stronger tail condition are not asserted here.

contents.name: Theorem 7.3.23 credible-ball coverage consequences
contents.reason: Credible-ball calibration is a downstream application and is not needed to establish the product-prior weak BvM limit in this pair.

sources.title: Kolyan Ray, Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, arXiv:1407.3397v3 (2016)
sources.locator: Full 48-page paper fetched and inspected. §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 5–8 (PDF pp. 7–8), define H(delta), its Gaussian white-noise law and the bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM notion; §7.1, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 23–25), gives a separate projection/tail proof for empirical and hierarchical prior procedures. Those prior assumptions differ from this pair's fixed product-prior theorem.

contents.name: §§2.1–2.2: white-noise topology H(delta), Gaussian law, and bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM definition
contents.reason: This independent paper confirms the same weak topology and white-noise target; the present definition and trace threshold are still justified explicitly in the local H(delta) items.

contents.name: §7.1: finite-projection decomposition and tail control for weak BvM with adaptive empirical and hierarchical priors
contents.reason: The projection-and-tail architecture independently checks the proof route, while the paper's empirical and hierarchical priors are not imported as hypotheses for this fixed product-prior theorem.

contents.name: Theorems 3.1–3.2: adaptive empirical-Bayes and hierarchical-Bayes claims with self-similarity and prior-specific rate assumptions
contents.reason: These are distinct adaptive-prior theorems with additional assumptions; this pair retains the controlling fixed product-prior theorem and does not assert adaptive BvM conclusions.
